$comment: Ground-truth fixtures from sub-phase 0.7. Every entry carries a `license`, which sub-phase 1.1 made a CI-enforced requirement for the whole corpus; this directory was written to that rule before the rule existed. Nothing here is derived from a third-party font or document: experiment A commits measurements of Microsoft's fonts, never their bytes.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/text/autofit/build-deck.ts, recomputed and read back through PowerPoint by tools/ground-truth/text/autofit/run.ps1; the per-face browser metrics it is compared against come from tools/ground-truth/text/autofit/measure-face-metrics.ts
entries.description: 3521 probes answering what PowerPoint does with a:normAutofit and a:spAutoFit, added in sub-phase 3.4. Measured by driving TextFrame2.AutoSize to force a recomputation, saving the deck, and reading the numbers PowerPoint wrote into its own file - which only works while the presentation has a window, because autofit runs in the layout path and a headless COM harness measures nothing. The ladder is 15 rungs, tried font scale descending and within one font scale the smaller reduction first: not the tallest rung that fits, which 771 probes refute. The effective size is round(nominal x fontScale) to a whole point with halves up, except that a fontScale of exactly 100% leaves a fractional size alone. lnSpcReduction is subtracted from the a:lnSpc percentage and the difference quantised afterwards, clamped at one per cent of the line box; an exact-point a:lnSpc ignores the reduction entirely, so such a paragraph cannot be autofitted shorter. a:spcPct paragraph spacing is a fraction of the scaled 1.2 line box and a:spcPts is used raw; spcFirstLastPara defaults false. The fit test is against the box height minus tIns and bIns. A stored scale is applied verbatim, is never snapped to a rung, and opening a file never recomputes it. The block height is (n-1) advances plus a last line of max(advance, 0.75 x advance + b x size) while the advance is inside C x size and the fitted value above it - closing the question sub-phase 3.2 left open; b and C are properties of the typeface, measured for six faces, and Chromium's TextMetrics cannot supply either. a:spAutoFit sets the shape height to the text height plus both insets times 1.0097657, the same constant on four faces, and leaves a shape alone when the target is within a couple of points of its current height.

entries.sourceNote: PowerPoint 365 rendered the corpus deck this entry names and exported each slide as a PNG; tools/ground-truth/render/fidelity/analyse.ts reduced it through tools/fidelity/metric/reduce.ts. The deck is ours and CC0-1.0; what is committed is a measurement of how PowerPoint drew it, at a resolution that retains no glyph outline and no image.
entries.description: 63 probes across four packages answering the image-fill questions of sub-phase 2.12. a:tile/@flip mirrors ALTERNATE tiles, so the visible period doubles - mirroring every tile scores 0.19 against 1.00. @algn puts one whole tile flush to that edge of the shape box, all nine values to the pixel, and @tx moves the lattice from there, positive right and down. A tile is sized from the FULL image at its own declared resolution, so a:srcRect changes what is drawn in a tile and not how big it is. a:grayscl, a:biLevel and a:duotone all weigh BT.709 in sRGB - BT.601 scores 0.32 against 0.999 - a:alphaModFix/@amt is an opacity rather than a transparency, a:lum is per channel with slope 1/(1-contrast) above zero and 1+contrast below it and a brightness term that grows with that slope, and a:clrChange matches exactly. Where the arithmetic rounds is not separable and both readings are scored.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/text/bullets/build-deck.ts, read back through PowerPoint by tools/ground-truth/text/bullets/read.ps1, which exports every slide as EMF so PowerPoint own ExtTextOutW calls can be read; the scheme vocabulary is cross-checked against what tools/ground-truth/text/bullets/author.ps1 made PowerPoint write for itself
entries.description: 6849 probes answering what PowerPoint draws for a:buChar, a:buAutoNum, a:buBlip and a:fld, and which of a:latin/a:ea/a:cs/a:sym draws each character, added in sub-phase 3.5. Measured by exporting each slide as EMF and reading the ExtTextOutW calls PowerPoint itself made, so a bullet comes back as the characters it drew with the face, size and colour it drew them in - identification by reading rather than by fitting a width. The 41 ST_TextAutonumberScheme values are PowerPoint own: its object model was walked from 0 to 47 and it wrote each accepted style into a package. Alphabetic numbering is not bijective base-26 - after z comes aa then aaa, the letter being (n-1) mod A repeated floor((n-1)/A)+1 times - and the counter wraps at 780 for five alphabets and at 392 for Hebrew, with Thai alone carrying an off-by-one. The East Asian zero is U+25CB and not U+3007, and the three East Asian families have three different ten-form rules. A symbol bullet is mapped through the Windows-1252 codepage byte and not the code point, so a U+2022 bullet in Wingdings draws U+F095 and not U+F022. a:buFont is inert for an autonumber, which is drawn in the first run face, while a:buClr and a:buSzPct do reach one. Numbers are in no file: a run is consecutive paragraphs at one level sharing a scheme and a startAt, deeper levels pass through it and shallower ones break it. A picture bullet is 0.7 x the font size tall and follows its own aspect ratio. Text on a bulleted first line starts at max(marL, -indent, bulletLeft + advance) where a positive indent moves nothing and the bullet is clamped to the frame; a wrapped line is at marL exactly. a:fld is recomputed on open for all 18 reserved types and the cached a:t is shown only for a type nothing reserves; the format is Windows own per-locale pattern keyed on the field lang, which Intl.DateTimeFormat reproduces on 25 of 97 readings.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/paint/colour/bases/build-deck.ts; the RGB values were sampled from PowerPoint's own rendering and the transparency from its object model
entries.description: 259 swatches answering the colour questions 0.7-C did not ask, added in sub-phase 2.6: a:scrgbClr is linear light and not sRGB percentages (14/14); a:hslClr uses the same bi-hexcone as the lum and sat transforms; the 147 ST_PresetColorVal names and the value PowerPoint paints for each, both the Gray and the Grey spelling; the thirty ST_SystemColorVal names on this machine, plus three probes showing that @lastClr does NOT win over the system value; alpha through Shape.Fill.Transparency; a crossed p:clrMap proving dk1/lt1/dk2/lt2 bypass it while the twelve mapped names follow it; and the Strict `60%` spelling of ST_Percentage accepted inside a Transitional part. One question per package, so a refusal names its own cause: 20 of the 21 decks opened with no repair, and the one that did not - an out-of-range a:hslClr/@hue - has its two swatches flagged fromRepairedDeck and excluded from every assertion.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/paint/colour/transforms/build-deck.ts; the RGB values were sampled from PowerPoint's own rendering
entries.description: 214 solid-fill swatches exercising every DrawingML colour transform, with the RGB PowerPoint painted for each. The deck was generated by tools/ground-truth/paint/colour/transforms/build-deck.ts and contains no third-party content. Sub-phase 2.6 resolves against these numbers rather than against a chosen linearization constant.

entries.sourceNote: a measurement of Microsoft-authored files, not a copy of them: header fields only, no font data and no glyph outlines
entries.description: The EOT header of all 76 ppt/fonts/*.fntdata parts across four decks PowerPoint saved, with subsetting on and off. Header fields only: no font data, no glyph outlines, nothing that is Microsoft's to license. The decks themselves are NOT committed, because they contain Microsoft's fonts. This is the fixture that settled experiment A - PowerPoint compresses every embedded font with MicroType Express.

entries.description: 144 probes across 23 packages answering the gradient and pattern questions of sub-phase 2.7. A gradient with two distinct colours and a stop at each end is NOT interpolated linearly - black to white paints BABABA at its midpoint, not 808080 - and the curve is measured rather than derived, no closed form fitting better than eight of 255 over 1920 samples; every other gradient is linear in sRGB to within a byte. The blend space is a plain 2.2 power, not the sRGB piecewise transfer and not linear light, cross-validated on five colour pairs. a:gsLst is sorted by @pos and PowerPoint writes its own from-centre fill unsorted. a:lin/@scaled bends the angle towards the long axis, not away from it. Path gradients put stop 0 at the focus, so nothing reverses; a:fillToRect behaves as a point at its centre; path=circle is a true circle reaching its last stop at the corner. The 54 ST_PresetPatternVal tiles, enumerated by PowerPoint itself and read pixel-exact at 96 DPI, three of them antialiased and lgGrid identical to cross. One question per package: seven of the fifteen hostile probes were refused, each attributed to itself.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/fonts/metrics/measure-in-browser.ts, which builds eleven fonts with tools/ground-truth/lib/truetype.ts and loads them into Chromium as data URIs, and scored by tools/ground-truth/fonts/metrics/analyse.ts against @pptx-studio/cli own font-table reader. No installed face is read: every probe family name exists nowhere, so an answer can only have come out of the bytes.
entries.description: Four questions a font-table reader must answer to stand in for a browser, added in sub-phase 3.10 so that `pptx-studio render` can measure text in Node. Each is settled by a font built to make the candidate readings disagree, which no real face does. The font bounding box comes from OS/2.usWinAscent and usWinDescent, except where fsSelection bit 7 is set and it comes from sTypoAscender and sTypoDescender - 22 of 22, where reading usWin alone scores 20, sTypo alone 12, and hhea, which every implementation reaches for first, scores 10. Pair kerning is read from GPOS when the font has a kern feature and from the legacy kern table otherwise - 66 of 66, where preferring the legacy table scores 60 and reading only it scores 54, so a reader that implements the simpler table alone is wrong on every font that carries both. A width is the sum of each glyph advance in font units, scaled by size over unitsPerEm, truncated to 1/65536 px, plus each kern adjustment rounded to the same step - 396 of 396 across eleven fonts, six strings and six sizes from 8px to 1000px, where exact float arithmetic scores 136, truncating both scores 388, and quantising the whole string once scores 264. The ideographic baseline is the BASE table ideo coordinate of the DFLT script, and the face box descent where there is none - 30 of 30, where the descent alone scores 22 and reading the coordinate of the script being measured scores 20; Chromium consults no other script when DFLT is absent, and hands back a coordinate outside the em as written. One font carries a second cmap, format 12 alongside format 4, mapping one code point above the BMP that format 4 cannot address at all: a reader must choose the subtable on merit rather than take the first it understands. The advance is linear in size to within 1.04e-4 px, so the browser does not hint it and a table reader can reproduce it; that is four orders of magnitude under the 0.149% median by which the same browser disagrees with PowerPoint in text-metrics.json.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/fonts/substitution/build-deck.ts, read back through PowerPoint by tools/ground-truth/fonts/substitution/read.ps1 over an EMF export of every slide (the LOGFONTW face name is what PowerPoint asked GDI for) with TextRange2.BoundWidth alongside it, and cross-examined in Chromium by tools/ground-truth/fonts/substitution/measure-in-browser.ts; scored by tools/ground-truth/fonts/substitution/analyse.ts
entries.description: Six questions about which typeface a run is actually drawn in, each fitting exactly one candidate reading, added in sub-phase 3.7. PowerPoint draws a Latin face it does not have in Calibri, whatever the name says - 22 of 22, against 17 for a reading that takes the style word out of the name and 20 for the theme own minor face - and lays it out with Calibri metrics exactly, all 12 width comparisons. Of the three hints CT_TextFont carries only @charset moves the answer: @panose and @pitchFamily are ignored across 14 probes, while charset 128 gives Yu Gothic and 178 gives Arial. +mj-lt names a:majorFont/a:latin and +mn-lt names a:minorFont/a:latin, 8 of 8 against 2 for the swapped reading, with substitution applied after the reference is followed. TextRange2.Font.Name reports the requested face, never the substituted one, in all 159 probes. In Chromium a family is absent when it measures equal to all three of monospace, serif and sans-serif stacked behind it: 38 of 38, where any single anchor scores 36-37 because the browser resolves each generic to a real face, and document.fonts.check scores 18 by answering yes to all 38 including the 20 that do not exist. The fingerprint is a word rather than three glyphs - no set of three or fewer single characters separates as many families, because Segoe UI and Leelawadee UI agree on every character measured - and is only comparable at one size, advances being non-linear in size by up to 11.1%. Chromium last resort for an unknown family is its own serif, not Calibri, so a font stack that does not name Calibri renders a missing face in the wrong one.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/text/frames/build-deck.ts, read back through PowerPoint by tools/ground-truth/text/frames/read.ps1 over TextRange2.BoundTop and BoundLeft per paragraph and per line, with an EMF export of every slide for the questions a bounding box cannot answer; the a:bodyPr vocabulary is cross-checked against what tools/ground-truth/text/frames/author.ps1 made PowerPoint write for itself
entries.description: 601 probes answering where a block of text sits inside a shape, how far in from each edge and which way it runs, added in sub-phase 3.6. Twenty-one questions, each fitting exactly one candidate reading. The insets default to 7.2/3.6/7.2/3.6 points per attribute and the anchor works inside the inset box, not the shape box. ST_TextAnchoringType has five values and PowerPoint implements three: just and dist lay out identically to b in all 190 readings, stretch nothing, and are reported by the object model as an anchor it has no name for. spcFirstLastPara decides more than the outer two paragraph gaps - with it off the block keeps only the trimmed last-line height 3.4 measured, and with it on the last line takes a full advance, which is 60 of 60 across five line spacings. anchorCtr centres the block along the line axis while anchor positions it along the stacking axis, and the two axes swap when the text is turned: vert and eaVert anchor from the right edge and align from the top, vert270 from the left and the bottom, mongolianVert from the left and the top. The insets do not rotate with the text - lIns always insets from the physical left edge. eaVert and mongolianVert ask GDI for the @-prefixed vertical face; vert and vert270 do not. vertOverflow=ellipsis replaces the whole first line that does not fit with a lone U+2026 rather than truncating it, clip stops laying out, and neither changes the height of the block. a:br starts no bullet, advances no autonumber, pays no spcBef or spcAft, does not reset the first-line indent, and its own a:rPr does not set the height of the line it begins. An empty paragraph is 1.2 x the a:endParaRPr size, which beats a:defRPr when the two disagree. A column is (frame - (n-1) x spcCol) / n wide. And a:bodyPr inherits per attribute through the placeholder chain from any level, so a bare a:bodyPr on a slide is not the schema default. A line whose bottom lands exactly on the frame edge is not drawn: a box exactly two line boxes tall shows one line.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/text/line-breaks/build-deck.ts and read back through PowerPoint by tools/ground-truth/text/line-breaks/read.ps1; the prefix widths that sized every probe box come from tools/ground-truth/text/line-breaks/measure-widths.ts
entries.description: 2188 probes answering where PowerPoint breaks a line, added in sub-phase 3.3. Measured by sizing a box to hold exactly n code points and reading back the text of line 1, so the break position is read rather than inferred from a width. The rule is not UAX#14 with tailoring: it is far smaller, and a faithful UAX#14 reading scores 1878/2212 where the measured rule scores 2212/2212. PowerPoint breaks after a space run, after a hyphen-minus, en dash, em dash or soft hyphen (only after - never before an em dash), between two East Asian characters and at a script transition, and nowhere else: not after a solidus, not anywhere in a URL or a Windows path, not at a ZERO WIDTH SPACE, and not inside a number at a comma, point, currency sign or percent. a:pPr/@latinLnBrk absent behaves as false where ECMA-376 gives it a default of true; @hangingPunct absent behaves as true; @eaLnBrk is inert. Trailing spaces are never charged to the fit test and a soft-hyphen break pays for the hyphen it draws. When no opportunity fits, the line force-breaks at exactly what does, and latinLnBrk="0" does not prevent it. The built-in kinsoku sets are measured one character at a time (71 may not begin a line, 19 may not end one, 6 hang) with six unrestricted controls, and disagree with the widely repeated list in four places. The file's p:kinsoku is ignored unless strictFirstAndLastChars="0", and then it replaces the built-in list entirely with nothing surviving. A p:kinsoku whose @lang is not East Asian makes PowerPoint refuse the package. Also records that PowerPoint segments Thai by dictionary, which we do not reproduce, and that Arabic prefix widths are not monotone.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/paint/lines/build-deck.ts; every position is a sub-pixel crossing of half coverage recovered from PowerPoint own slide export, in points on a 960x540pt slide, with the dash and arrowhead packages exported at 3840 wide so a run boundary is located to about a tenth of a pixel; the emitted JSON is passed through prettier before committing, as every generated file in this repository is
entries.description: 213 probes across 47 packages answering the stroke and effect questions of sub-phase 2.8. The eleven preset dash arrays are exactly the ones everyone quotes, confirmed three ways: measured from the crossings, cross-checked against an explicit a:custDash of each quoted array, and shown to scale with @w at 3, 6 and 24 points. a:ln/@cap defaults to flat and not to the square ECMA-376 specifies, and PowerPoint writes @cap for only two of its twelve dash styles, so that default governs almost every line in every deck. A cap does not lengthen a dash: PowerPoint compensates so the painted period is unchanged, which means an SVG dasharray needs each dash shortened by one width and each gap lengthened by one. The join defaults to round, not to SVG’s miter, and the default miter limit is 8 - bracketed between a corner of ratio 7.91 that paints a full miter and one of 8.01 that does not - with @lim measured against the whole stroke width rather than half of it. The five compound forms subdivide @w and sum to exactly one width. The six arrowheads are sm=2, med=3, lg=5 stroke widths for both @len and @w, confirmed on all 54 combinations and at three stroke widths, with a diamond and an oval centred on the line endpoint while the other three put their tip on it, and a stealth distinguished from the triangle it shares a silhouette with only by a notch a quarter of its length. Every blurred edge in DrawingML is one operator with one constant: sigma = r/3 across fourteen measurements on four elements, isotropic to 0/255, with a glow growing the edge and a soft edge shrinking it by 0.9r and a glow using half the radius it declares. a:prstShdw, which the plan for this sub-phase does not mention and no open renderer implements, is written by PowerPoint for twenty of its forty-three shadow presets, and what each of the twenty paints is recorded here. One question per package: thirteen of the fifteen hostile probes were refused, each attributed to itself, so the stroke vocabulary is validated far more strictly than the fill vocabulary was.

entries.sourceNote: tools/ground-truth/render/pictures/build-deck.ts wrote the deck and its four-quadrant image, PowerPoint 365 exported the slide as a BMP through tools/ground-truth/render/pictures/read.ps1, and tools/ground-truth/render/pictures/write-tables.ts reduced it to the colours below. The deck and the image are ours and CC0-1.0.
entries.description: 54 samples over 9 probes answering what the p:pic container does, added in sub-phase 2.13. Exactly one of twenty-four readings survives and all twenty-three rivals are refuted at a full channel: a non-rect prstGeom CLIPS the image rather than merely bounding it, p:blipFill BEATS a fill written beside it in p:spPr, flipH and flipV mirror the IMAGE and not only the outline, and a:ln on a picture is drawn WHOLLY OUTSIDE the box - 12pt out and none in, of a 12pt line, where the same line on a p:sp straddles the geometry at 6 and 6. The corpus could not have answered any of this: all 26 of its pictures are an unrotated, unflipped, unoutlined prst=rect with no competing fill.

entries.sourceNote: a measurement of two decks PowerPoint wrote from content we authored; the decks are not committed and none of their content is
entries.description: What Microsoft's own serializer writes, measured across 38 XML parts: no BOM, one declaration form followed by CRLF, 1305 self-closing tags all written tight and none spaced, only the three entity references, no part broken across lines, and no xml:space on an a:t that begins and ends with spaces. The fourth entity, ", is a follow-up measurement taken on 2026-08-27 against the same build: E8's two decks contained no attribute with a quote in it, and a shape renamed through COM to a "quoted" name was saved as name="a "quoted" name". Plus the ZIP conventions - general-purpose flag 0x0006, no UTF-8 flag, DOS timestamp zeroed to 1980-01-01, and a 520-byte 0xa220 Open Packaging growth-hint extra field. Also settles experiment E6: build 20326 still writes the mc:AlternateContent wrapper with Requires="v" but no vmlDrawing part and no @spid, and the embedded workbook is a package relationship to an .xlsx rather than a CFB .bin. None of this is derivable from the schema, and sub-phase 0.5's byte gate is a statement about all of it.
probe.ttf wrapped in an uncompressed EOT version 0x00010000, charset 1, names not NUL-terminated. PowerPoint 365 does not render it, which is half of experiment B's finding.

The probe font wrapped in an uncompressed EOT version 0x00020002 with NUL-terminated FamilyName and StyleName, charset 0, and the full v2.2 tail - byte-for-byte the header shape PowerPoint itself writes, differing only in that the payload is not compressed. PowerPoint 365 does not render it either, which is the core of experiment B's finding. Family name is 'ProbeCharlie'. Every benchmark deck embeds this file.

A synthetic TrueType font whose eight letters are solid bars of increasing height, so a rendering of ABCDEFGH is a staircase no substitute font can imitate. Accepted and rendered exactly by Chromium's OTS sanitiser and by Windows GDI+. Family name 'ProbeAlpha' exists nowhere, which is what makes it a valid test of whether an embedded font was used.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/model/build-deck.ts; the positions and colours were read out of PowerPoint through its own object model rather than measured from a bitmap
entries.description: 114 probes in 37 packages answering which sheet a shape inherits from, and what. A placeholder that states no geometry still has a position, so every candidate parent sits in a rectangle no other candidate shares and the rectangle a probe lands in names the parent it matched. The headline is that the two hops do not use the same key and neither uses the pair every implementation assumes: slide to layout matches on @idx alone (34/34, against 13/34 for (type, idx)), and layout to master matches on the folded type, taking the first placeholder of that type. Also: a bare <p:ph/> is obj at idx 0; a slide master accepts only title, body, dt, ftr, sldNum and hdr; every master must own its own theme part; p:bgRef and a:fillRef index the same two style lists with the same 1000 offset, where 0 and 1000 mean none and out of range clamps to the last; a layout’s overrideClrMapping reaches the slides bound to it and a slide’s own beats it; and fills, lines and p:style descend the same chain as geometry, all the way to the master. 23 of the packages are hostile and each is alone in its own file; 16 were refused or repaired.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/text/cascade/build-deck.ts; every value was read out of PowerPoint through its own object model rather than measured from a bitmap, because a run whose a:rPr declares nothing still has a resolved size and Font.Size reports it; the emitted JSON is passed through prettier before committing, as every generated file in this repository is
entries.description: 129 probes in 39 packages answering which of the nine claimed sources of a text property PowerPoint reads, in what order, and which it ignores. A ladder of nine packages, each declaring one rung fewer than the last, makes the reported font size name the level that won; scored over all 40320 permutations, none fits while a placeholder is assumed to read every source, and exactly one order fits once the two it ignores are dropped: a:rPr, a:pPr/a:defRPr, the shape's a:lstStyle, each ancestor placeholder's a:lstStyle, then the master's p:txStyles. Three claimed sources turn out not to be sources at all - a:objectDefaults, a:defPPr and p:otherStyle, the last of which nothing measurable reads. The bucket is selected by the @type at the *end* of the inheritance chain rather than the shape's own (37/37 against 13/37 for the reading every implementation uses), dt/ftr/sldNum reach no bucket and fall through to p:defaultTextStyle where a body placeholder ignores it, @marL and @indent default to 0 rather than to the schema's 347663 and -342900, properties merge per property across levels rather than the nearest level winning outright, and the Strict `150%` spelling of ST_Percentage is accepted inside a Transitional part. Also committed: PowerPoint's own built-in p:txStyles, substituted wholesale when a master declares none. 2 of the 39 packages were repaired - a slide may not carry a sldImg or hdr placeholder - and their 4 probes are excluded from every score.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/text/metrics/build-deck.ts and read back through PowerPoint by tools/ground-truth/text/metrics/read.ps1; the browser column comes from tools/ground-truth/text/metrics/measure-in-browser.ts
entries.description: 2091 probes answering what a line box is, added in sub-phase 3.2. The line advance is a font-independent 1.2 x the font size across 13 faces and 7 sizes (worst spread 0.00003pt); a:lnSpc percent multiplies that line box and not the font size (463/463 against 66/463), while a:spcPts is used raw (against 397/463 for scaling it by 1.2); the percentage is rounded half up to a whole percent before use, so val=106667 is 107% (371/371, against ceil 365 and floor 359); a block is (n-1) x advance + the last line, which is not the advance; a:rPr/@spc is absolute points applied after every character including the last (18/18); a:rPr/@kern is an inclusive minimum font size and kern=0 means never (12/12 against 5/12 and 8/12 for the boolean readings). Also records what Chromium measureText disagrees with PowerPoint by (median 0.15%, p95 0.70%), that TextRange2.BoundWidth includes a trailing paragraph mark one space wide, and that PowerPoint measures an uninstalled Latin face as Calibri while document.fonts.check reported it present.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/render/text/build-deck.ts, read back through PowerPoint by tools/ground-truth/render/text/read.ps1 - TextRange2 line boxes from the object model, the world transform and per-character advances from an EMF export of every slide, and a 1920x1080 bitmap where the question is about ink - with Chromium font boxes and its own text-decoration geometry from tools/ground-truth/render/text/measure-in-browser.ts; scored by tools/ground-truth/render/text/analyse.ts
entries.description: Fifteen questions about where PowerPoint puts the glyphs, fourteen fitting exactly one candidate reading and one refuting every cheap implementation, added in sub-phase 3.8. A flipped shape never mirrors its text: flipH is ignored outright and flipV turns the whole block 180 degrees about the frame centre, 20 of 20, where counter-flipping both axes scores 10 and mirroring the glyphs scores 5. The text turns by the shape rotation plus a:bodyPr/@rot, and @upright="1" drops the shape rotation while keeping the frame extents swapped when that rotation snaps to 90 or 270 - 19 of 19 and 5 of 5. A line box is 1.2 times the largest size on it, 36 of 36 where the first run scores 34 and the smallest 32, and the next line top is one of this line boxes below this one, 9 of 9. The baseline sits inside the 1.2 line box at the typeface own ascent-to-descent proportion, 36 of 36 across eight faces and four sizes, where the CSS half-leading model every browser uses scores 9 and a face-independent fraction scores 12; sub-phase 3.4 per-face autofit coefficient scores 24, failing only on Courier New whose natural line box exceeds 1.2. Alignment anchors the line without whatever spaces it ends with, which hang past the edge, 21 of 21; dist stretches the last line of a paragraph and just, justLow and thaiDist do not. A decoration scales with the em, 18 of 18, stops at the last glyph rather than running under a trailing space, and sits where the typeface says - Courier New underline is 0.2347 em below the baseline and Tahoma is 0.0842 - so neither of the two cheap implementations survives: Chromium own text-decoration is 0 of 16 on both offset and thickness, drawing every face at 0.05 em and 0.1 em, and one offset for all eight faces is 4 of 16. A run with a:rPr/@baseline rises by that percentage of the size it asked for and is drawn at two thirds of it, 4 of 4; cap="small" uppercases at four fifths, 3 of 3. A line is shaped as one string and a run boundary splits only the drawing call, so a kern crosses it - 6 of 6, against 4 for shaping each run alone.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/render/transforms/build-deck.ts and tools/ground-truth/render/transforms/analyse.ts; every composed position was read out of PowerPoint through its own object model, and the fill extents were solved from a reference ramp on the same slide
entries.description: 65 probes across 15 packages measuring what a p:grpSp does to the shapes inside it: the child coordinate map (ext/chExt scaling, chOff offset, and what a zero or a missing chOff/chExt mean), the order a rotation and a mirror compose in, how a group turn composes with a child turn, what happens to a rotated child when the group scales the two axes differently, whether a group scales stroke width, the rectangle a:grpFill lays the enclosing group fill out over, and what a slide shows that it did not write. Includes what PowerPoint itself wrote when asked to mirror an already-rotated shape and to ungroup a rotated, mirrored group.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/text/vertical-glyphs/build-deck.ts, read back through PowerPoint by tools/ground-truth/text/vertical-glyphs/read.ps1 over an EMF export for the exact pen, face and per-character advance and a BMP export at four pixels to the point for the one thing a drawing stream cannot say, which way the outline points; the metric a browser can reproduce comes from tools/ground-truth/text/vertical-glyphs/measure-in-browser.ts
entries.description: 87 probes answering what happens to a glyph inside a frame that has been turned, added in sub-phase 3.6 after eaVert had been laid out but refused rather than drawn. A glyph keeps its own orientation in an eaVert or mongolianVert frame if and only if it is in the a:ea slot, 45 of 45: PowerPoint asks GDI for the @-prefixed vertical variant of the face for that stretch and for the plain face beside it, so a Latin run in an eaVert frame turns with the line exactly as it does in a vert frame. The choice is per script run and not per frame, 32 of 32 over eight mixed strings. Halfwidth katakana is the one stretch drawn with ETO_GLYPH_INDEX, so its record carries glyph ids rather than characters. Neither the layout nor the advance changes: the line pitch is 1.2 of the em on all five faces, read from two pens rather than a bounding box, and the cell pitch is the face advance in every direction. An upright glyph sits with its alphabetic baseline one less the ideographic baseline down its cell and its own x origin at the centre of the line box, which is exact on the three faces whose cell is one em - Yu Gothic 0.0002, MS Gothic 0.0010 and SimSun 0.0004 along, MS Gothic 0.0006 and SimSun 0.0013 across - and is 0.0391 out across on Yu Gothic. Microsoft YaHei and Malgun Gothic have a cell of 1.1027 and 1.1200 of the em rather than one, and neither reading fits them: 0.1125 and 0.1620 along, 0.1498 and 0.0924 across. Meiryo, Yu Mincho and BIZ UDGothic were dropped after the drawing stream named a substitute rather than the face the file asked for.

entries.sourceNote: generated by tools/ground-truth/text/wordart-columns/build-deck.ts, read back through PowerPoint by tools/ground-truth/text/wordart-columns/read.ps1 over an EMF export for the exact pen and face and a BMP export at four pixels to the point for which way the outline points; the font box the cell is fitted against comes from tools/ground-truth/text/wordart-columns/measure-in-browser.ts, because that is the only box the renderer can read
entries.description: sixty-seven probes answering the one thing the two WordArt directions need and no other direction has: the cell each character is stacked in. It is square - the pitch down a column is the width of the column, 49 of 49 - and it is seven sixths of the font box, exact to four ten-thousandths of the em on Arial, Courier New, Times New Roman, Verdana, Segoe UI, MS Gothic and Malgun Gothic. It is not the em, not 1.2 of the em, and not the widest advance in the run; all three are scored and all three miss every row. Inside the cell a glyph keeps the orientation it has in a horizontal frame, 6 of 6 against the bitmap, drawn from the plain face and never the @-prefixed one, 51 of 51: its advance box is centred across the cell and its baseline sits the face descent up from the cell floor, 9 of 9 within a fortieth of the em. A column holds as many cells as the frame has room for and breaks mid-word to do it. wordArtVert stacks its columns rightward from the left edge and wordArtVertRtl leftward from the right, 6 of 6. Two faces are recorded rather than ruled: Chromium reports a font box for Yu Gothic and SimSun that is not the one PowerPoint measured from, so their columns come out 0.2582 and 0.0446 of the em narrow and no browser-visible metric closes the gap. A column of two sizes stacks each run in a cell of its own size, 2 of 2, while every glyph in it is centred across the widest cell in the column rather than its own, 2 of 2. PowerPoint rounds the cell before stacking, by a hundredth of the em at twelve points and a two-hundredth at eighteen and twenty-eight.
